papers.title: EthicalAI: An Evidence-Linked Ontology of AI Integrity Failures

changelog: Four rigor improvements: validated the principle partition (Section 4.2, codebook kappa 0.42/0.38 vs the category 0.90/0.83, reported as only moderately reproducible); added the harm axis (causes) over the grounded 207; added a comparison table vs MIT Risk Repository/OWASP/Malberg; and characterized the typed relation graph (533 relates_to, 38 maps_to, 24 is_a, 16 opposite_of) as a lightweight ontology.

Extended the principle partition from the grounded 207 to all 434: classified the 227 proposed analogies into the seven operational principles from their definitions and filled their violates field. Section 3.3 now reports the grounded/proposed/total split with a stacked Figure 1 (honesty 112, calibration 100, non-maleficence 52, transparency 51, scope-fidelity 50, independence 43, corrigibility 26; sum 434).

Added the principle layers derived from the behaviours (new Section 3.3 + Figure 1): the six top-level charter principles, and seven operational obligations read off the per-record violates relation that form a verified clean partition of the 207 (honesty 67, calibration 45, non-maleficence 31, transparency 25, scope-fidelity 15, independence 14, corrigibility 10).
Reframed as an ontology paper, per the author's decision that the paper's subject is the ontology of unethical AI behaviours, not the citation-grounding finding.

Cut the citation-grounding finding entirely: the five-class typology, Figure 1, the LLM-citation probe, and the two-check framing. New title, abstract, introduction and conclusion lead with the ontology (record structure, eleven-category scheme, relation semantics, evidence-linking). Kept the grounding and category-recoverability results as validation. 5,287 -> 3,447 words.
Aligned with the companion benchmark paper: consistent 'companion auditing paper' naming and the companion's title named once.

Grounded the paper in the user's Six Principles of Ethical AI. Added contracts/ethical-principles.md (the canonical charter, above the AI Integrity Contract), and framed the citation-grounding finding as operationalising the honesty-and-transparency principle, descriptively rather than as a bolted-on manifesto (slop judge 4/10 -> fixed).
The charter is referenced in the introduction as motivation and in Section 8 among the artifacts.

De-slop pass toward a human scientific register. AI-slop judge 4/10 -> 2/10, all seven prior structural tells resolved: cut the 'three things to reuse' contribution list and 'This paper delivers' package sentence, replaced 'sits next to' / 'Its proposed value is that', consolidated the per-section scope disclaimers, unstacked the causes-relation negations, and rewrote the conclusion to close the opening problem instead of paraphrasing the abstract.
Judge verdict: reads primarily as human scientific prose. Every verified number preserved.

Submission roadmap Stage 6: produced the submission PDF (docs/paper.pdf) via pandoc + tectonic, with a native LaTeX/TikZ Figure 1 replacing the web SVG. 12-page PDF, all nine sections, Figure 1, and twelve references. arXiv/workshop ready.

Submission roadmap Stage 5 (writing polish): differentiated the conclusion from the abstract (no verbatim finding restatement; ends on the forward-looking rule plus the machine contrast); pinned the OWASP living-document citation with an accessed date. Length 5,219 words.
Submission roadmap Stage 4: four-reviewer council re-review (peer minor-revision up from major; every number reconciles; ai-writing 2/10; one groundedness BLOCK).

Re-grounded the LLM-citation probe to the saved run data (gpt-4o 40/45 declined, 5/5 fabricated; deepseek 7/8), committed both per-prompt jsonls; moved Figure 1 into the markdown source; consolidated the repeated scope disclaimer; cut the Section 3 meta-announcement; reframed the surface-match/machine link as a contrast. Rejected one flag after verifying a number was correct at the pinned commit.

Submission roadmap Stage 3: added Figure 1, an inline SVG bar chart of the five-class citation-failure distribution (surface-match dominates), with a caption and an in-text reference. Counts match the Section 3.1 table.
Submission roadmap Stage 2: added a second-model probe. deepseek-chat never declined (0/45, vs gpt-4o's 85%) and fabricated 7 of 8 verified suggestions, reusing one arXiv id across unrelated modes.

The two models fail in opposite styles (over-cautious vs over-confident) but neither produces a citation trustworthy without resolving the source. Abstract, Section 3 probe paragraph, and the probe writeup updated.

Submission roadmap Stage 1: citation integrity sweep. Verified all 12 references resolve to real papers on arXiv (titles, authors, years); fixed Agrawal's author list; confirmed Spracklen's 2025 is the USENIX venue year.
Added a Section 8 note that every reference was resolved to its source before inclusion, the same discipline the paper applies to the catalogue.
Paper-orchestra agent council revision (architect, literature, section writers, integrator, groundedness verifier), validated before publishing.

Promoted the citation-grounding result to its own Section 3 and named the five-class failure typology (surface-match, scope-mismatch, misfiling, polarity-reversal, wrong-population) so it is a citable object.

Positioned against the closest prior work with five arXiv-verified citations: Lewis 2020 (RAG), Rashkin 2021 (AIS attribution), Liu 2023 (verifiability audit), Gao 2023 (ALCE), Agrawal 2023 (reference hallucination).
Added the LLM-citation probe: asked for references, GPT-4o declined on 55 of 65 prompts, and all 10 confident suggestions bound a plausible title to an arXiv id for an unrelated paper.
Converted the keyword/LLM hook from an (ungrounded) analogy into a measured small-probe result; earlier groundedness BLOCK resolved.
Added the citation-failure typology that turns the headline error rate into a diagnosis.
Applied the review council's convergent fixes: reframed 29/50 as a count not a rate, stated the binning rule, added the kappa small-n caveat, fixed a source batch-arithmetic bug.
Reframed to lead with the transferable finding and the reader payoff instead of a flat construction log.
Consolidated the defensive disclaimer cadence flagged by the AI-writing review.
Honest, map-led resource paper: the historical 207-record study, the citation audit, and the verification sweep.
Baseline before this improvement cycle.

papers.title: Contracts Between Humans and AI Agents

changelog: Added Figure 1 (specificity by review condition, from Table 2), aligning with the ontology paper's figure. The focused judge conditions roughly double specificity over bulk clause review at equal recall. Bars transcribed exactly from the table.

Verified the four flagged 2025/2026 preprint citations against their sources (three confirmed on arXiv; one DOI resolves but is bot-blocked, left as the prior correction). Added the companion paper's 'each reference resolved to its source' note for alignment.

Cleared the last AI-slop residues (judge 2/10, reads as human-written): moved the charter reference out of the Section 2 argument into the reproduction section with a locator, and restated the Section 3.2 defensive aside positively.

De-slopped to a human scientific register (AI-slop judge 4/10 -> fixed): removed the desk-reject-risk internal charter file path from the intro, cut the 'X not Y' disclaimer cadence from seven to one, compressed the Section 3.2 metadata and Section 3.1 unimplemented-components paragraphs into Limitations pointers, and reordered the conclusion.
Aligned with the ontology paper: reciprocal cross-reference and a shared scope register.

Grounded in the Six Principles of Ethical AI: the Principal/Agent/Auditor division realises principle 5 (Human Accountability and Oversight), and the audit serves principle 6 (Integrity Under Pressure). Descriptive, anchored in the introduction and Section 2.
Now published as its own live page (benchmark-paper.html) alongside the ontology paper.
Companion method paper: the clause-judge vs baselines ablation on six hard suites.
Honest result: decomposition buys specificity, the named catalogue buys traceability; no dominance or SOTA claim.
